title: Position Needs an Origin and a Direction
subject: Physics
objective: "200 m" means nothing until you say from where and which way. Position is a signed number with a unit, measured from a chosen origin.

fill.q: The fixed point from which position is measured is called the ____.
Positions on the side opposite to the chosen positive direction are ____.
A position is written as a sign, a number and a ____.
Changing the origin changes positions but not the ____.

tf.q: "The shop is 200 m away" fully describes the shop's position.
tf.explain: It needs an origin and a direction.

tf.q: A position of −150 m means the object is on the negative side of the origin.
Moving the origin changes the displacement between two places.
tf.explain: Displacement = final − initial; the shift cancels.

tf.q: The origin itself is at position 0.
tf.explain: Every position is measured from it.

ar.r: The sign tells on which side of the origin the object lies.

ar.a: The displacement from home to shop is +200 m for any origin.
ar.r: Displacement is the difference of two positions measured from the same origin.
ar.explain: Shifting the origin shifts both positions equally.

mcq.q: Home is the origin, right is positive. A school 150 m to the left is at:
With home as origin the shop is at +200 m. With the school (−150 m) as origin, the shop is at:
Which does not depend on the choice of origin?
mcq.explain: It is a difference of positions.

mcq.q: To describe a position on a straight road you need:
options: an origin, a direction, a number and a unit

num.q: With home as origin, the shop is at +200 m and the school at −150 m. Find the distance between the school and the shop.
Take the school as origin. Find the positions of home and shop, and the displacement home → shop.
num.answer: Home +150 m, shop +350 m, displacement +200 m

short.q: Why is "200 m" not a complete position?
short.solution: It does not say from where (origin) or in which direction (sign); the same 200 m could be left or right of any point.

short.q: Explain why changing the origin does not change displacement.
short.solution: Moving the origin adds the same amount to every position, so the difference between two positions (the displacement) stays the same.
